meta.note: The two-day window overlaps with yesterday's edition, so several strong pieces already ran there. The State of Brand sitemap returned 11 pages, none published inside the window. General AI news (Meta Muse, UN and US AI policy, security) dominated the international feeds without a link to creative work.

stories.title: Unexplained variance, not slowness, breaks trust in AI products
stories.blurb: Users judge an AI tool against the fastest response they have personally seen, so a normal six-second run reads as broken after a two-second one. The author builds tools on top of AI chat products and argues the interface has to reset that anchor instead of promising speed.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: The variance problem in AI products

stories.title: An identity animated by captured sign language
stories.blurb: Templo built the DeafCity Hub identity from motion-captured British Sign Language gestures and creative coding, so every brand movement comes from a real hand rather than keyframed animation. The pink and orange palette was picked to stand apart from other Deaf-led identities.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Templo’s visual identity for DeafCity Hub is a fusion of creative coding, British sign language and gestural motion capture

stories.title: McLaren takes its new wordmark from a 1920s garage sign
stories.blurb: The lighter sans-serif wordmark references the sign above the McLaren family service station in Auckland. The old speedmark stays, but only for the racing and golf sub-brands.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: McLaren’s new logo looks like a luxury fashion brand

stories.title: A design congress identity that refuses to play safe
stories.blurb: Everyday Practice's identity for World Design Congress 2027 in Seoul runs on clashing colours, scattered shapes and a seesaw-like logo in motion. Creative Bloq's argument: design events have drifted to one typeface and one colour, and this shows how far such a brief can go.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: This out-there branding is the bravest design I've seen all year

stories.title: Converse pulls an ad after a projected logo read as a hood
stories.blurb: A star logo projected onto a white skirt, plus a tight crop that left the shoes dangling, was read as KKK and lynching imagery. Converse apologised and removed the image; the open question is how it passed approval.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Converse forced to remove ad over racist allegations

stories.title: Skoda's Peaq: restraint that has to look deliberate
stories.blurb: Design Week argues that at £52k and without a big grille, every surface has to work harder, and credits the aligned light and bumper lines and a drag coefficient of 0.249. The review also records the flush door handles that retracted and briefly locked the reviewer out.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Design Review: Skoda goes big on the Peaq

stories.title: Design Council puts UK design at £136.7bn as strategists move up
stories.blurb: Creative Boom's monthly roundup cites the Design Council figure, up 40% since 2019, and senior strategy hires at Pearlfisher and FutureBrand. Studios are betting on AI in two directions: specialist hires or more senior people.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Booms Shakes: September s biggest hires, bold bets on AI, and design overtakes retail

stories.title: The Chase buys Squad to plan its succession
stories.blurb: The Manchester consultancy acquires Squad through a share exchange and fully takes over The Chase Films, while co-founder Ben Casey steps back to co-chair. The deal adds a consumer portfolio to a B2B and public sector client base.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: The Chase s co-founder Ben Casey steps back as Squad s founders take the reins

stories.title: Anthropic and OpenAI compete on price, not capability
stories.blurb: Opus 5.5 costs $4/$20 per million tokens, 20% below Opus 5, and Anthropic claims about 40% lower real-world cost; GPT-6 Sol and Luna halve prices against their predecessors. Ars Technica reads both launches as a response to cheaper open-weight models and model routers.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: New Anthropic, OpenAI models make same promise: A little more for a lot less money

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Anthropic releases Opus 5.5 with lower prices and Fable-level performance

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, boasting lower cost and fewer mistakes

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5 with stricter safeguards for cybersecurity

stories.title: A model that answers design system questions with numbers
stories.blurb: TypeSafe's Jev returns calibrated probabilities for choice and yes/no questions and writes no text at all. TJ Pitre ran it against a 135-component library: 36 of 40 casually phrased descriptions hit the right component on the first guess.

sources.name: TJ Pitre (Southleft)
sources.headline: The AI That Refuses to Write a Sentence
